sourcedFrom:
TAURUS TX 22
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: Taurus's TX22 book covers the TX22 and the TX22 Competition together - same .22 LR action, different barrel and slide length - and it publishes a five-step field strip that is NOT the same as the centrefire Taurus pistols'. The TX22's slide comes off FORWARD after a half-inch push, and its barrel drops out of the slide downward rather than lifting up. Rimfire fouling is waxy and heavy, so this is a gun that earns a strip more often than its round count suggests.

steps.title: TX22 or TX22 Competition - and which safety yours has
steps.action: Check the barrel first: the standard TX22 is 4.1 inches and 7.06 overall, the Competition is 5.25 and 8.21 with a red dot mounting system on it. Both are .22 LR, single action, 16 or 10 rounds. Then look at the left side of the frame for a manual safety lever, because Taurus fits one only on certain TX22 models.
steps.prose: The two builds share this manual and share every step below, but they do not share an optics story - the Competition's red dot mounts to a base on the BARREL, not the slide, which is why its optic does not reciprocate. Knowing which gun is on the bench before you start also tells you whether the safety lever you are about to check even exists.
steps.cite:
TAURUS TX 22
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Specifications, printed p.15 (PDF p.8)

steps.title: The manual safety is optional on the TX22 - find out before you rely on it
steps.action: If your TX22 has the ambidextrous manual safety, put it fully into Safe now and confirm it goes all the way, not half way. If it has no lever, note that and do not go looking for one; Taurus fits it on certain TX22 models only, and the striker block and trigger safety are what every TX22 carries.
steps.prose: The reason to settle this at the start is that a half-engaged lever is worse than none - it feels like a safety and blocks nothing. Taurus is explicit that it has to be all the way in the Safe position and not at some other point in its travel, and on a light polymer .22 the lever is easy to knock into the middle without noticing.
steps.caution: Taurus lists the TX22's safety devices as striker block, trigger safety and manual safety on certain models only - so on a TX22 without the lever, the only mechanical safeties are internal.
steps.quote: 2. Manual Safety (on certain TX22 models). If your firearm is equipped with, always use the manual safety. When you need it to work, it needs to be all the way in the Safe position, not half way or at some other point in its travel.
steps.cite:
TAURUS TX 22
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Firearms Safety Systems, printed p.8 (PDF p.5)

steps.title: Magazine out, slide locked back, look and feel both
steps.action: Muzzle safe and finger off the trigger, press the magazine release beside the trigger guard and pull the magazine. Lock the slide back on the slide catch, then look into the chamber and the magazine well and put a finger in each.
steps.prose: A .22 LR case is small enough to sit in a TX22 chamber and read as a shadow, and the rim can hang on the extractor after the slide has cycled, so the eye alone is genuinely not enough here. Do the magazine first - the TX22's 16-round magazine holds a high stack and racking before it is out just chambers another round.
steps.quote: 1. Before disassembly always (1) Keep your finger off or the trigger, (2) point the muzzle in a safe direction (3) remove the magazine by pressing the magazine release button (4) pull the slide to the rear and lock it back and (5) look and feel the magazine well and chamber to confirm the pistol is empty. An empty firearm cannot fire.
steps.cite:
TAURUS TX 22
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Disassembly, printed p.28 (PDF p.15)
steps.warn: After removing the magazine, always check the chamber and make sure it is empty.

steps.title: The TX22 fires with the magazine out
steps.action: Do not treat the magazine leaving the gun as making it safe. Taurus states these pistols have no magazine disconnect and will fire with the magazine removed, and the strip below requires a deliberate trigger press.
steps.prose: This bites harder on a rimfire than people expect, because .22 ammunition is handled casually and a single loose round chambered from a range session is easy to forget. The chamber check is the only thing that makes the trigger press at the next step a safe act rather than a gamble.
steps.quote:
These Taurus pistols do not have a magazine disconnect (safety). They are capable of firing with 
magazine removed.
steps.cite:
TAURUS TX 22
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Operating Instructions, printed p.27 (PDF p.14)

steps.title: Disassembly latch straight down - no slide movement needed
steps.action: Hold the pistol with four fingers over the slide and your thumb on the rear of the grip, and pull the disassembly latch on the left of the frame straight down with your other hand. Then release the latch.
steps.prose: Note what this step does NOT ask for: unlike the Taurus G3 and TH pistols, the TX22 does not want the slide drawn back an eighth of an inch first. Trying to hold the slide back while rotating the latch is the usual reason a TX22 feels stiff to take down - the latch wants the slide fully forward and at rest.
steps.quote:
2. Hold the pistol in your hand in such a way that four fingers rest over the slide and your thumb rests on the rear of the grip. With 
the other hand, pull the disassembly latch down. Release the 
disassembly latch.
steps.cite:
TAURUS TX 22
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Disassembly, printed p.28 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: Trigger pulled, slide FORWARD half an inch, then lift it off
steps.action: With the pistol confirmed empty, pull the trigger and release it. Push the slide forward about half an inch and lift it up off the grip - forward and then up, which is the opposite order to most striker pistols.
steps.prose: That half inch takes the slide's rails past the frame's rail cuts so it can lift clear; less than that and it will not come off, more and it fouls the barrel. This is the step where the earlier chamber check pays for itself, because the trigger press is unavoidable on a single-action TX22.
steps.quote:
3. Pull and release the trigger. Push the slide 
forward 1/2" and lift the slide off the grip.
steps.cite:
TAURUS TX 22
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Disassembly, printed p.28 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly off the bottom of the barrel
steps.action: Turn the slide over and lift the recoil spring assembly out of its seat under the barrel, keeping a hand over it. It is captive and is never dismantled.
steps.prose: The TX22's spring is light compared with a 9mm's - this is a blowback .22 - but it is short, and short springs jump further when they escape. Let the tension off progressively rather than plucking the assembly out of its seat.
steps.quote:
4. Release the recoil spring assembly from its 
position on the bottom of the barrel.
steps.cite:
TAURUS TX 22
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Disassembly, printed p.28 (PDF p.15)
steps.warn: Please take care to prevent the forcible ejection of the slide spring assembly plate and compressed slide spring assembly.

steps.title: Barrel out of the slide - front and DOWN
steps.action: Pull the barrel forward inside the slide and take it out DOWNWARD. Down is the direction on a TX22; the centrefire Taurus pistols come out upward, and forcing this one up will bind it against the slide.
steps.prose: That leaves four pieces: frame, slide, barrel, recoil spring assembly. On a Competition model the optic base rides on the barrel, so the sight comes off the gun with the barrel and its zero is unaffected by the strip - do not loosen the optic screws to get the barrel free.
steps.quote:
5. Remove the barrel from the slide by pulling it to 
the front and down.
steps.cite:
TAURUS TX 22
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Disassembly, printed p.28 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: If a suppressor collar is fitted, that is a wrench job and not part of the strip
steps.action: Leave the muzzle hardware alone during a routine clean. Taurus's TX22 ships with a 1/2-28 suppressor adapter collar, and swapping it means a 3/8 inch wrench to remove the thread collar and a 9/16 inch wrench to tighten the adapter - not fingers, and not during a wipe-down.
steps.prose: The reason this belongs in a cleaning guide at all is ammunition: Taurus says to use only subsonic or standard velocity ammunition when a suppressor is fitted, and subsonic .22 leaves noticeably more soft fouling in the bore and on the breech face. A suppressed TX22 needs the brush more often, not less.
steps.quote: Only use subsonic or standard velocity ammunition in your pistol when using a suppressor.
steps.cite:
TAURUS TX 22
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Suppressor Adapter Collar Installation, printed p.32 (PDF p.17)

steps.title: Oil film, clear bore, dry crevices - what Taurus asks of a TX22
steps.action: Keep the pistol covered with a light film of good quality oil and the bore clean and free of debris. Wipe it with a lightly oiled cloth, do the same through the bore, take the excess off, and brush the dust out of the crevices with a small clean brush.
steps.prose: Rimfire changes the emphasis: .22 LR is unjacketed and lubricated with wax, so the fouling is soft, sticky and everywhere - the breech face, the extractor claw and the underside of the slide collect it faster than the bore does. That is also why 'excess oil should be removed' is not a throwaway line here; oil plus wax makes a paste that gums a light blowback slide.
steps.quote:
In order to keep a firearm safe to use, it must be 
kept clean and covered with a light film of good 
quality oil to prevent corrosion. The barrel bore 
should be cleaned and left free of debris.
steps.cite:
TAURUS TX 22
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.34 (PDF p.18)

steps.title: This procedure is for a TX22 and nothing that resembles one
steps.action: Before you put it back together, note that none of this transfers. Taurus warns that firearms which look alike differ in the location and function of their controls, and the TX22's forward-off slide and downward-out barrel are the clearest example of it in their own catalog.
steps.prose: A shooter who owns a TX22 and a G3 has two Taurus pistols with a disassembly latch in the same place that come apart in opposite directions. Read the latch, then read the direction - if pulling the slide forward does nothing, you are holding the other gun.
steps.quote:
FIREARMS ARE NOT ALL ALIKE
Many makes and models of firearms might LOOK nearly the same. However, they differ widely in design, operation, and in the location and function of various controls.
steps.cite:
TAURUS TX 22
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Ammunition, printed p.23 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel and recoil spring assembly. That is the TX22 field strip in full, and Taurus stops the owner there - the striker, the striker block, the extractor and the sear stay in the slide and frame.
steps.prose: The book does publish two further owner procedures that are not part of a clean: the magazine strip, which Deep Clean walks, and the reversible magazine release, which is a handedness change rather than maintenance. Everything else routes to a qualified gunsmith.
steps.quote:
No further disassembly is recommended unless done by a 
qualified gunsmith.
steps.cite:
TAURUS TX 22
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Disassembly, printed p.29 (PDF p.15)

deepSteps.title: Punch the base retainer and run the base cap forward
deepSteps.action: Press a punch onto the magazine base retainer through the hole in the base cap and hold it in, then slide the base cap toward the FRONT of the magazine. Keep a thumb over the cap as it leaves the tube.
deepSteps.prose: The TX22's magazine is a tube with a loading button riding in a slot down the side, so the follower is captured by that button and cannot simply fall out - the strip has an extra move the centrefire magazines do not. Expect the spring to be long and lively for a .22; sixteen rounds of stack is a lot of coil in a narrow tube.
deepSteps.quote:
1) To disassemble, use a punch to press in on the magazine  
base retainer.
deepSteps.cite:
TAURUS TX 22
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Magazine Disassembly / Assembly, printed p.30 (PDF p.16)
deepSteps.warn: Use care to prevent the forcible ejection of the magazine base retainer and compressed magazine spring.

deepSteps.title: Spring out, follower to the bottom, then push the loading button free
deepSteps.action: Withdraw the base retainer and the spring from the tube, turn the magazine upside down until the follower is at the lowest position, then push the magazine loading button out of the follower and lift the follower out. Assemble in reverse order.
deepSteps.prose: The follower has to be at the bottom of its travel before the button will come out, because that is the only point where the button clears the end of the slot. Forcing it anywhere else chews the button's stem, and a TX22 with a damaged loading button is a magazine you can no longer thumb down to load.
deepSteps.caution: Brush the tube dry and leave it dry. Waxy .22 fouling plus oil is exactly the mixture that makes a follower hang halfway up a full magazine.
deepSteps.quote:
3) Withdraw the magazine base retainer and magazine spring 
from magazine tube. Turn the magazine upside down until the 
follower is in the lowest position. Push the magazine loading 
button out of the follower and remove the follower.
deepSteps.cite:
TAURUS TX 22
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Magazine Disassembly / Assembly, printed p.30 (PDF p.16)

cleaning.name: BORE, CHAMBER & BREECH FACE
tasks: Run a .22 brush wet with solvent through the bore from the chamber end, then a dry patch - the barrel is out of the slide, so nothing needs to touch the crown
Scrub the chamber mouth and leade: unjacketed .22 leaves a hard ring there that grows until extraction gets sticky
Clean the breech face and under the extractor claw with a brush; waxy rimfire fouling packs in behind the claw and causes failures to extract
Hold the barrel to a light and look through it before it goes back

cleaning.name: SLIDE, RAILS & FRAME
tasks: Wipe the slide interior and the frame rails with a lightly oiled cloth, then take the excess off
Brush dust and residue out of the crevices with a small clean brush
Check the disassembly latch moves freely and the slide catch is clean - a fouled latch is what makes a TX22 feel seized at takedown
On a Competition model, wipe around the barrel-mounted optic base but do not loosen its screws

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES & MUZZLE
tasks: Wipe magazine bodies externally, work the loading button up and down and confirm it runs the full slot
If a suppressor adapter collar is fitted, check it is still tight by hand and inspect the 1/2-28 threads for damage
A pistol with a laser must not be cleaned in a well or ultrasonic machine that submerges it

reassembly: Insert the barrel in the slide and guide it to the rearmost position.
Insert the recoil spring assembly into the slide over the barrel, compressing the spring slightly to get it into position.
Line up the slide's rail cuts with the rails on the frame, push the slide gently down onto the frame and rack it back - the disassembly latch will latch back in place on its own.
Cycle the slide several times with no magazine inserted and no rounds in the chamber to confirm the barrel / slide / frame relationship is correct.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty: the slide should run its full stroke on the light blowback spring and close fully under its own power; the disassembly latch must be back up and captured; the trigger should reset audibly as the slide returns; the slide catch should hold on an empty magazine; and if your TX22 has the manual safety, it must move fully to Safe and fully to Fire with no middle detent. On a Competition model, confirm the red dot is still tight on its barrel-mounted base before the pistol is fired.
